docs.title: Let's Begin
docs.text:
Markdown is a simple markup language for formatting documents easily. Benefits of markdown for documentation are its simplistic to focus on the narrative you are writing and ability to run almost anywhere without issue.

We recommend using Visual Code for writing Markdown documents

docs.title: GitHub Cloning and Branching
docs.text:
To begin using the E-Waste Battery Extraction documentation application MkDocs you have to clone the repository first. 

git clone git@github.com:222038631/e-waste-battery-extraction-UAT.git
Once cloned please create a branch starting with - docs/

docs.title: Navigating The File System
docs.text:
When creating your first document, locate your respected sub-team folder and began your first Markdown file adventure.

We encourage to create sub-folders within your respected team folders to further organise your documentation by any category you wish. MkDocs will automatically demonstrate a clearer presentation of those categories.

Importing Images

MkDocs and Markdown support image processing in your documents. Please note if you are adding images please add them into your sub-teams respected image folders to maintain a clear repository.

E-Waste Battery Extract Documents

│   ├── Computer-Vision

docs.title: Your First Document
docs.text:
To create your first markdown document you simple need to rename an empty file type to .md 

example.md

PDF to Markdown

If you have already created documentations within a Word or PDF format, there are online options available to convert PDF to Markdown.

Opening the markdown file in any code editor (e.g., visual code) and begin typing your document.

Spell-Check Enabled

It is recommended to have spell-check plugins enabled on your code editors when writing Markdown if you wish.

docs.title: The following below are the Markdown syntax:
docs.text:
# Heading

## Sub-Heading

### Sub-Sub-Heading

![Alt Text](Image File Path)

- List Item
    - Sub-List Item
* List Item
- [] Checklist Item
- [x] Checklist Item

docs.title: Viewing Markdown in the Browser
docs.text:
Not all code editors or web-browser may render MarkDown correctly. To resolve this your code editors may have add-ons/plugins to allow appropriate viewing (Visual Code is recommended).

Otherwise within your web-browser there are extensions that will render Markdown appropriately.

Additionally, you may run mkdocs locally if you wish to see how your document would appear in MkDocs.

Run MkDocs Locally

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
The Battery Extraction Project utilises the GitHub documentation system to showcase and maintain all documentation within regard to the project.

To maintain the documentation creating a fork of the Redback repository is required inline with appropriate company standard operating procedures.

If the Redback repository cannot be accesses/unable to fork/or missing files please clone all the files from the following repoitory below,

docs.title: Setting up the Site
docs.text:
The repository contains an automated script to allow for re-creation of the website a user pushes anything to the repository.

  1. Once the files/repoitory have been copied/or forked, ensure you rename the following folder - "RENAME" to ".github".

  2. Commit and Push all the files onced complete.

  3. Accessing the GitHub Settings -> Pages tab select "gh-pages" under the branch tab, than press save.

  4. Under the Settings -> Rules, create a rule for the main branch and selecting the following options

    • Restrict Deletion
    • Require a Pull Request Before Mergign
    • Block Force Pushes

This will ensure all students must create a branch to request merging of documents rather than merging to the main branch.

docs.title: Local Environment
docs.text: If you wish to run MkDocs locally to see how your document may appear in GitHub without using other tools such as Markdown extensions the below steps outline the Python setup process.

docs.title: Linux
docs.text:
You will need to clone the repoistory first.

  1. Creating virtual Python environment 
    python3 -m venv env
  2. Activate the environment 
    source env/bin/activation
  3. Install Mkdocs and supporting libraries 
    pip3 install mkdocs mkdocs-material mkdocs-awesome-pages-plugin

The following command runs MkDocs local instance with live reloading of any page changes. 

mkdocs serve --livereload

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text: The robotic controls require installation of an Ubuntu 24.04 Virtual Machine (VM) alongside the required libraries. The following robotic arm control code is written in Python for easy interoperation and modification, aimed to allow any IT/Robotic field student to continue development without in-depth knowledge of ROS2, MoveIt, or Matlab/Simulink.

docs.title: Virtual Machine Installation
docs.text: ISO: Ubuntu 24.04 - https://ubuntu.com/download/alternative-downloads RAM: 8GB Storage: 40GB

docs.title: Application Installation
docs.text: Install ROS2 and MoveIt! from the following documentation,

docs.title: ROS2
docs.text: https://docs.ros.org/en/jazzy/Installation/Ubuntu-Install-Debs.html

docs.title: MoveIt!
docs.text: https://moveit.picknik.ai/main/doc/tutorials/getting_started/getting_started.html

docs.title: GitHub Clone
docs.text: Clone the following repository within the VM or move the files into the VM. https://github.com/BeardedSwitchDragon/SysSims-EwasteExtraction

docs.title: Using the Controls
docs.text:
Ensure ROS2 and MoveIt respected files are sourced to allow running within the command line.

source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash source ~/ws_moveit/install/setup.bash

Run the following MoveIt command to open the simulated robotic arm.

ros2 launch moveit_servo demo_ros_api.launch.py ros2 run moveit_servo servo_keyboard_input

Run the following Python script within another terminal instance (Ensure all terminal instances are sourced for ROS2 and MoveIt Python3 main.py
